Reviewer recommends rejection: All checked claims are confirmed against opened sources, and the primary-source warning is cleared by the Feb 2026 interview. Reject only because no official club or federation source could be opened, so the page adds no value over existing pages. Re-review after an official source is accessible.

claims.claim: Interim charge in January 2026 after Ruben Amorim was sacked
claims.note: IANS (opened): 'took interim charge after Ruben Amorim was sacked in January'.

claims.claim: Permanent appointment on Friday 22 May 2026, contract to 2028
claims.note: beIN (opened): permanent manager confirmed 'this Friday' with contract until 2028; date matches URL 2026-05-22, a Friday.

claims.claim: He was 44 when the deal was announced
claims.note: IANS: 'The 44-year-old took interim charge'.

claims.claim: He now manages the club he played for
claims.note: Both report him continuing as head coach.

claims.claim: Retired as a player in 2018
claims.note: Archive gives retirement 13/05/2018; IANS says he joined the coaching staff when he retired in 2018.

claims.claim: First match 2-0 v Manchester City; 3-2 v Arsenal; wins over Liverpool, Chelsea, Aston Villa, Tottenham; no scores for last four
claims.note: beIN (opened): 2-0 v City, 3-2 v Arsenal, then Liverpool, Chelsea, Aston Villa, Tottenham with no scores given.

claims.claim: Results against lower-profile teams were not as decisive
claims.note: beIN, verbatim: 'results against lower-profile teams were not as decisive'.

claims.claim: Premier League Manager of the Month after the City and Arsenal wins
claims.note: IANS (opened): 'awarded the Premier League Manager of the Month award'. The link to the first two games is from the Football365 summary, not a verbatim quote.

claims.claim: Interview with The Football Interview, Feb 2026: job is 'the ultimate role'
claims.note: Vanguard, 20 Feb 2026 (opened): 'For me, it's the ultimate role,' Carrick said.

claims.claim: United won 11 of 16 games
claims.note: IANS verbatim: 'with 11 wins from 16 games'.

claims.claim: Highest Premier League points tally since his arrival
claims.note: IANS verbatim: 'accumulating the highest points tally in the Premier League'. Attribution changed from club to press.

claims.claim: Moved the side from seventh to third and secured Champions League football
claims.note: beIN verbatim: 'from seventh to third place, securing qualification for the Champions League'. Football365 confirms the Champions League qualification.

claims.claim: beIN: achievement of bringing the club back to the Champions League 'should not be underestimated'
claims.note: beIN verbatim, in the article's own narration. Attribution corrected from Wilcox to beIN.

claims.claim: Form under Carrick left United little choice but to appoint him
claims.note: Football365 verbatim: 'left them little choice but to appoint the former midfielder'.

claims.claim: Wilcox: approach 'aligns with the club's values, traditions and history'
claims.note: IANS: this sentence is in Wilcox's quoted remarks. Citation moved to IANS.

claims.claim: Wilcox: Carrick 'has forged a strong bond with the players'
claims.note: IANS: Wilcox quote, verbatim.

claims.claim: Wilcox: 'Michael has thoroughly earned the opportunity to continue leading our men's team'
claims.note: IANS: attributed to Wilcox, verbatim.

claims.claim: Carrick: responsibility of leading the club 'fills me with immense pride'
claims.note: Football365 verbatim: 'Carrying the responsibility of leading our special football club fills me with immense pride.'

claims.claim: Carrick: 'past five months' and 'resilience, togetherness and determination'
claims.note: Football365 verbatim.

claims.claim: Carrick: 'From the moment that I arrived here 20 years ago, I felt the magic of Manchester United'
claims.note: IANS verbatim (also beIN).

claims.claim: Carrick: 'deserve to be challenging for the biggest honours again'
claims.note: Football365 verbatim.

claims.claim: Came through the West Ham United academy
claims.note: Archive: 'came through the youth academy' at West Ham United.

claims.claim: Midfield performances earned a 2004 move to Tottenham; loans at Swindon and Birmingham
claims.note: Archive verbatim: 'His performances in midfield earned him a move to Tottenham Hotspur in 2004'; loans listed (no dates given).

claims.claim: Signed from Tottenham on 31 July 2006 for £18.6m
claims.note: Archive: transferred from Tottenham 31/07/2006, £18.6m. Ferguson is no longer named as the signer.

claims.claim: Ferguson saw him as the perfect replacement for Roy Keane
claims.note: Archive verbatim.

claims.claim: Debut 23 August 2006, 3-0 win at Charlton Athletic
claims.note: Archive: 23/08/2006, Charlton (A), won 3-0.

claims.claim: Retired 13 May 2018 aged 36; 464 appearances and 24 goals
claims.note: Archive: retirement 13/05/2018; 464 apps and 24 goals. Football365 confirms 464 games. Age 36 is correct from DOB.
Archive lists the five seasons; Football365 says five PL titles.

claims.claim: PFA Team of the Year 2012-13
claims.note: Archive.

claims.claim: Champions League and FIFA Club World Cup both in 2008
claims.note: Archive.

claims.claim: League Cup 2010 and 2017; FA Cup 2016
claims.note: Archive. The manutd search snippet says three League Cups from a fan site; not used.

claims.claim: UEFA Europa League among honours with the club
claims.note: Football365 verbatim list of honours.

claims.claim: IANS: former England international
claims.note: IANS verbatim.

claims.claim: 34 England caps
claims.note: Archive: 'earned 34 caps for England'.

claims.claim: Competed for a place with Gerrard and Lampard; calm presence and tactical intelligence valued by England staff and players
claims.note: Archive verbatim for both parts.

claims.claim: Joined first-team coaching staff under Mourinho, then Solskjaer
claims.note: IANS verbatim.

claims.claim: Caretaker manager when Solskjaer left
claims.note: IANS verbatim: 'as caretaker manager'. No year given in the article.

claims.claim: Managed Middlesbrough from October 2022; second permanent job
claims.note: IANS verbatim: from October 2022, two-and-a-half years. beIN: 'three years' and 'second permanent challenge'. Sources disagree on duration; the article now says so.

claims.claim: Turned 45 on 28 July 2026
claims.note: DOB 28 July 1981 per archive; arithmetic is correct.

claims.claim: Twelve seasons as a midfielder for the club before retiring in 2018 (summary)
claims.note: 2006 to 2018 is twelve seasons.
